items.claim: The single-verse boundary at Prov.28.14 is warranted: the verse is skeleton-tier isolated from both neighbors and its blessing/hardened-heart antithesis is self-contained.
items.evidence: An independent stoplist-filtered skeleton re-sweep of Prov.28.13-Prov.28.14 and Prov.28.14-Prov.28.15 finds zero shared content tokens in either direction, matching chapter 28s 0/27 catchword-adjacency count in the staged inventory. Both named neighbors are equally non-adjacent-cohesive, so the single named rival (28:15) is not a strawman pick in a chapter with no real rival candidate.

items.claim: The atomic call at Prov.28.20 holds: no catchword bridges either neighbor and the rejected-alternative treatment is accurate.
items.evidence: Re-swept skeleton tokens for Prov.28.19-Prov.28.20 and Prov.28.20-Prov.28.21 share no content token (the campaign stoplist correctly excludes the bare negative particle common to several verses in this stretch). The named rival, a merge with 28:21, is correctly rejected: the two sentences share no root or construction.

items.claim: The Prov.28.27 boundary is well warranted: zero shared content tokens with either neighbor and no disclosure-inventory entry on the verse.
items.evidence: Skeleton re-sweep of Prov.28.26-Prov.28.27 and Prov.28.27-Prov.28.28 confirms no shared tokens, consistent with chapter 28s 0/27 catchword-adjacency count. The disclosure inventory (marks/paseq/K-Q/x-small-nun) carries no entry at Prov.28.27, matching the rows own claim.

items.claim: The rejection of a Prov.29.2/29.3 cluster is the correct call: the shared root is real but is a single, stem-different token joining two otherwise unrelated subjects, below the cluster bar.
items.evidence: Re-sweep confirms the only chapter-29 catchword-adjacency hit touching this verse is the יִשְׂמַ֣ח/יְשַׂמַּ֣ח pair with 29:3, matching the staged inventorys 2-pair count for chapter 29 (the other pair, at 29:26/29:27, does not touch this row). The two pointed forms differ (יִשְׂמַ֣ח Qal vs יְשַׂמַּ֣ח Piel, byte-verified in verse_map_oshb.json), so even the shared skeleton token is not a repeated identical form. The disclosed non-adjacent opener echo with Prov.29.16 is byte-confirmed (both verses open בִּרְב֣וֹת) and is correctly used only as texture: a cluster cannot skip the fourteen intervening verses to join them.

items.claim: The atomic call at Prov.29.3 is correct and symmetric with the 29:2 treatment; the one candidate catchword is thin and the domestic/political subjects genuinely diverge.
items.evidence: The shared יְשַׂמַּ֣ח token with 29:2 is the rows own disclosed and rejected candidate, byte-verified at both pointed forms. Toward 29:4 the only near-repeat is the generic noun for man (bare in 29:3, waw-prefixed in 29:4), which is not an exact skeleton match and is the same class of high-frequency noun the same writer part correctly treats as too generic to cluster on elsewhere in this chapter (the analogous shared-noun pair at 29:26/29:27); its non-disclosure here is not a defect.

items.claim: The Prov.29.8 boundary call is sound; the wisdom-root echo with 29:9 is correctly downgraded from adjacency evidence to texture.
items.evidence: Skeleton re-sweep finds no shared token with Prov.29.7. The plural/prefixed wise-men form in 29:8 and the bare singular wise-man form opening 29:9 are confirmed NOT an exact skeleton match, so the rows characterization of it as a plural/singular mismatch rather than a catchword pair is byte-accurate and matches the staged inventory (no 29:8/29:9 entry in the 2-pair chapter-29 catchword-adjacency count).

items.claim: The row misdescribes its own verses parallelism class: it calls Prov.29.14 non-antithetic and synthetic in the rationale and device_notes, then calls it its own antithesis in the rejected-alternative sentence, though the boundary verdict itself is independently correct.
items.evidence: The verse is a single protasis-apodosis clause (מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן, verse_map_oshb.json) with no antithetic but structure, matching the rows own not a two-party antithesis and Synthetic parallelism language -- yet the rejected_alternative field asserts the verse already completes its own antithesis, contradicting the rows own literary-form classification on the exact question this lens reviews. The underlying atomic call is unaffected: an independent skeleton re-sweep confirms zero shared content tokens with Prov.29.13 or Prov.29.15, and the king-noun count (2 sites in this writer part, at 29:4 and 29:14, both מֶ֗לֶךְ/מֶ֤לֶךְ segol-patach noun pointing rather than the qamats reign-verb form) is byte-verified.

items.claim: The Prov.29.21 atomic call and hapax disclosure are both byte-verified and correctly kept separate from the boundary-confidence question.
items.evidence: Book-wide skeleton and word-bound sweeps of the verses final noun each return exactly 1 verse (Prov.29.21 only), confirming the rows hapax claim. No shared content token exists with Prov.29.20 or Prov.29.22, and the verse carries no PE/SAMEKH/paseq/K-Q disclosure-inventory entry.
